newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Accor to sign $100 mln deal with Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Accor to sign $100 mln deal with Morocco.

text.p: French group Accor will sign a convention with Morocco on Thursday to set up a $100 million international fund to upgrade tourism in the country, a senior official said on Wednesday.
The convention covers investments for existing tourist assets, as well as new projects, he added.
A market analyst said the group is eyeing investments in hotels and other leisure facilities in the tourist cities of Marrakesh and Fez, in southern and central Morocco.
Earlier this month, Morocco offered for sale nine hotels at a total minimum price of 95.9 million dirhams ($11 million), the privatisation ministry had said.

The hotels are mainly sited in the south, including the tourist city of Marrakesh. Two are in Chefchaouen and Oujda, respectively, in the north and east and one in the Atlantic port city of Casablanca.

Morocco plans to complete the sale of 114 companies by 1998. It has already sold stakes in 46 enterprises, including at least 18 hotels, since privatisation started in November 1993. ($1 =8.6 dirhams)
